post.description:
§5: JSON body (text path) — or multipart with an audio blob + the same
fields (voice path, create_log_voice above), which is the only way to get
the capture_failure response.

schema.title: Response Create Log Endpoint Api Logs Post

delete.description:
§5: discard a staged log — status 'discarded' is adherence-relevant
data (§9), so sheet close must land here, not just drop client state.

patch.description:
§9: staged_ms has exactly one write path — this one — and it writes
only while NULL, so the first render's timing can never be overwritten.

delete.description:
§7.1: removing a staged row writes item_resolutions.status='removed'
immediately, so the staging error stays visible in telemetry without
waiting for commit (commit-time absence remains the backstop). A removed
row never writes an alias and never reaches entries.

post.description:
Photo → vision → the identical cascade + staging; input_mode='photo'.
Idempotent by client id like POST /api/logs (§8.6). `tz` is optional —
without it the meal is inferred in the settings timezone.

The non-streaming entry. The + sheet's photo lane goes through the chat
(POST /api/agent, §6.4) since 2026-09-08 and shares `_stage_photo` with
this route; nothing here changed with it.

get.description:
The foods this account has logged, newest first, one per food, capped
at foods_repo.RECENT_FOODS_CAP (200) — the Search lane's "previously
added" list (§7.4). Every hit is already cached (food_id set), so a pick
goes straight to /api/logs/from-food. Declared before /api/foods/{food_id}
so the literal path wins.

schema.title: Response List Recent Foods Api Foods Recent Get

get.description:
Active macros; include_inactive=1 adds the deactivated ones (the
Library lists them under "inactive" with a reactivate action, §8.4).

schema.title: Response List Meals Api Meals Get

delete.description: §8.4: delete = deactivate. Idempotent; the row stays.

post.description:
"Save as meal": the macro's items are the log's committed entries
(food, serving, qty as committed). Create-or-update by name, so saying
"save this as my usual breakfast" twice updates the one macro.

Text: a same-id retry re-attaches to its live run; else the claim
before the stream, then the agent's events → `done`. The multipart form
(audio + the same fields) is the other content type on this path, as for
POST /api/logs.

history.description: JSON array of AgentTurn — the chat so far (§6.4)

image.description: a plate photo — the §3.4b lane as a chat turn; exactly one of audio or image

text.description: said alongside an image — makes it a chat turn the agent can see (§6.4)

photo_log_id.description: the staged photo log this conversation is tuning (§3.4b)

lat.description: the phone's latitude when the photo was taken

lng.description: the phone's longitude when the photo was taken

accuracy.description: how far off that fix may be, in meters

200.description: A stream of newline-delimited JSON events, one AgentEvent per line, ending with `done` or `error`.

schema.title: Response List Keys Api Keys Get

AgentDoneEvent.title: AgentDoneEvent
AgentDoneEvent.description:
The last event of a successful run: what POST /api/logs would have
answered. `replay` (§8.6): a same-id retry answered from the stored log
rather than a run this request made or attached to — no tool lines and no
reply came with it (the reply is not stored, BACKLOG 139).

AgentErrorEvent.title: AgentErrorEvent
AgentErrorEvent.description: The last event of a failed run, with the HTTP status it would have been.

AgentEvent.title: AgentEvent
AgentEvent.description: One line of the POST /api/agent stream.

AgentOutcome.title: AgentOutcome
AgentOutcome.description:
What the agent lane did with the utterance (§6.4): its one-sentence
reply, the weigh-in it recorded, if any, the answers it offers when the
reply is a clarifying question (`options`, tappable in the chat), and the
earlier staged logs it discarded because this turn replaces them
(`discarded`). Staged items ride the LogResponse as on any other log.
Assembled from what the tools did, never from what the model said.

AgentReplyEvent.title: AgentReplyEvent
AgentReplyEvent.description:
The agent's reply — or its clarifying question, when `options` carries
the 2–4 answers the chat offers as chips (§6.4).

AgentToolCallEvent.title: AgentToolCallEvent
AgentToolCallEvent.description:
The agent called a tool: `name` (log_food, log_estimate, log_weight,
discard_log, past_foods, save_meal, update_meal, adjust_photo, web_search)
with `args` as the model passed them. `read_photo` and `look_up` are the
exceptions — no model called them: the photo turn (§3.4b) emits each pair
itself so the chat can show the vision call and the lookups while they run.

AgentToolResultEvent.title: AgentToolResultEvent
AgentToolResultEvent.description:
What the tool answered (sanitized: never macros — the staged list shows
those). For web_search: the sources it consulted.

AgentTranscriptEvent.title: AgentTranscriptEvent
AgentTranscriptEvent.description: The spoken utterance as transcribed — the chat's user bubble (voice only).

AgentTurn.title: AgentTurn
AgentTurn.description:
One earlier turn of the Agent chat (§6.4), as the client remembers it:
what the person said, what the agent replied, and — for a turn that
staged a log — the log's id, its rows in words (never macros) and where
it stands, so a follow-up ("actually I only had half") can name it.

AliasRow.title: AliasRow
AliasRow.description: One aliases row ⋈ its food (route-local response shape).

Answer.title: Answer
Answer.description:
A tapped id-bearing option (source + source_id, or a cached food_id,
plus label) or free text.

BarcodeFood.title: BarcodeFood
BarcodeFood.description:
The cached food a barcode resolved to — enough to render the pick and
to call /api/logs/from-food with its id.

BodyProfile.title: BodyProfile
BodyProfile.description:
settings.body — every field optional so a partially filled wizard can be
saved; the compute endpoint requires the full set (GoalInputs).

CaptureFailureResponse.title: CaptureFailureResponse
CaptureFailureResponse.description:
§5: an audio log whose transcript came back empty/near-empty. The
client prompts retype; the logs row records the failure so the §9
telemetry counter increments. NEVER returned as an empty staged log.

CommitItemError.title: CommitItemError
CommitItemError.description:
One core-macros refusal (§3.5): the item stayed uncommitted as
needs_input; the rest of the log committed.

CommitRequestIn.title: CommitRequestIn
CommitRequestIn.description:
CommitRequest + the §3.5 step-4 / §8.4 "Save as meal" tap: the staging
sheet names the meal and the commit creates/updates the macro from the
items it writes (route-local, additive over models.py).

CommitResponse.title: CommitResponse
CommitResponse.description:
DayTotals + per-item refusals. A 200 with non-empty errors is a PARTIAL
commit — the client must keep refused rows visible (verify-me / pending),
never close over them (§3.5; the silent-protein-hole failure class).
The totals are for the day the entries landed on (§7.2 when-shift aware).

DayTotals.title: DayTotals
DayTotals.description: Consumed totals for the day vs targets (§5: commit response, diary).

DiaryEntry.title: DiaryEntry
DiaryEntry.description:
Response-only shape (route-local; the wire contracts live in models.py).
The display fields default to None because routes/entries.py builds this
model too (it has no source/web_source at hand).

EntryPatch.title: EntryPatch
EntryPatch.description:
Any subset: qty scales; serving_id re-derives; food_id corrects + learns;
meal refiles the entry under another meal and leaves the portion alone.

FoodHit.title: FoodHit
FoodHit.description: One condensed search hit — enough to render a row and to select it.

LogCreateResponse.title: LogCreateResponse
LogCreateResponse.description:
POST /api/logs: LogResponse + what the agent's meal tools did (§8.4):
`saved_meal` when a save landed, `note` when it lands at commit or could
not — never a silently empty staging list. `agent` carries the agent's
reply (§6.4) — with zero items it is what the client shows instead of a
sheet.

LogPollResponse.title: LogPollResponse
LogPollResponse.description: LogResponse whose items can carry the watchdog's stale flag.

Macros.title: Macros
Macros.description: §5: core macros required, fiber optional, extra micros allowed (all numeric).

MealItemOut.title: MealItemOut
MealItemOut.description: Stored item + display fields from the foods cache (Library rendering).

MealPatch.title: MealPatch
MealPatch.description: Any subset. trigger_phrases/items REPLACE the stored lists.

NutrientRow.title: NutrientRow
NutrientRow.description:
One nutrient as the source reported it. ``basis`` is the denominator:
per 100 g / 100 ml for FDC foodNutrients, per serving for branded label
panels and web-transcribed values.

OuraSync.title: OuraSync
OuraSync.description: One sync's outcome — also POST /api/oura/sync's answer.

SavedMealNote.title: SavedMealNote
SavedMealNote.description:
A macro this request created/updated (§8.4) — enough for the client to
confirm it ("Saved as 'usual breakfast' · 3 items").

ServingOption.title: ServingOption
ServingOption.description:
One row of foods.servings, surfaced on staged rows so the §7.1 portion
sheet can list every serving the database defines — with per-single-serving
macros for the live preview.

SettingsUpdate.title: SettingsUpdate
SettingsUpdate.description: PUT body: every field optional; only fields present are written.

StagedItemOut.title: StagedItemOut
StagedItemOut.description:
A StagedItem as returned by GET /api/logs/{id}, plus the watchdog flag.

stale=true marks a status="searching" item whose tier-3 run started (or
was staged) more than 60s ago with tier3_attempts < 2: the client should
re-kick it once via POST /api/resolve/tier3 (§3.4 failure lifecycle).
Computed at poll time, never persisted; null/absent everywhere else.

WebSource.title: WebSource
WebSource.description:
§3.4a: the citation for a web-transcribed (chain) food — the UI must
render it as a visible, clickable link (OpenAI usage-terms requirement).
